title: Two hidden traits in one seed
hook: Each hidden form shows in some seeds. How often do both show at once?

knows: offspring get one copy of a gene from each parent
a hidden (recessive) form shows only with two copies; two carriers give it 1 in 4 of the time
doesNotKnow: that two independently inherited genes combine by multiplying chances
how to read a two-gene grid of egg x pollen pairings

misconception: Showing both recessive traits has the same 1 in 4 chance as showing one.
objective: The learner can explain that with two separately inherited genes, each recessive form shows in 4 of 16 equally likely seeds but both together in only 1 of 16 (1/4 x 1/4).

claims.text: A parent carrying one dominant and one hidden copy of each of two separately inherited genes makes four equally likely egg or pollen types, so a cross of two such parents has 16 equally likely pairings.
claims.source: Mendel's law of independent assortment (Griffiths et al., Introduction to Genetic Analysis, ch. 3); enumeration in Demo.tsx (GAMETES x GAMETES).

claims.text: In that cross, white flowers show in 4 of 16 seeds, wrinkled seeds in 4 of 16, and both together in 1 of 16.
claims.source: Demo.tsx COUNT (white 4, wrinkled 4, both 1), counted from the grid it draws; 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16 (the 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio).

claims.text: Because the genes are inherited separately, a quarter of the white seeds are also wrinkled; independent chances multiply.
claims.source: Of the 4 white squares in the grid, exactly 1 is wrinkled (Demo.tsx). Product rule for independent events.

claims.text: Genes that sit close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together and break the 1-in-16 rule.
claims.source: Genetic linkage (Griffiths et al., Introduction to Genetic Analysis, ch. 4). Independent assortment holds for genes on different chromosomes or far apart on one.

claims.text: The plant is made up; purple over white and round over wrinkled are complete dominance, and every pairing is equally likely. Stated on the stage before the prediction.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #34. (Mendel's peas had these traits, but the lesson does not claim so.)

recall.question: Two genes are inherited separately. A child has a 1 in 4 chance of one recessive trait and a 1 in 4 chance of the other. Chance of both?
recall.why: Separately inherited chances multiply: a quarter of a quarter is one sixteenth.
